title: Trajectory policy graph for safe model wave deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a new policy engine to represent canary and A/B rollout strategies as a directed trajectory policy graph (TPG). The TPG should encode step schedules, conditional transitions driven by SLOs/metrics, shadow traffic forks, and automatic rollback paths. The goal is a declarative, composable configuration format that operators can author in the Console or API and that the serving runtime can execute with deterministic safety checks. This ticket covers design, a reference implementation of the evaluator, integration hooks for telemetry and Console, and an initial set of guardrail predicates (latency, error-rate, model-quality drift).
acceptance_criteria: TPG schema RFC written and reviewed (schema covers nodes: step, fork, wait, measure, rollback, converge)
Runtime evaluator implemented that can parse TPG JSON and produce deterministic traffic-split actions for a demo Canary flow
SLO-driven transition predicates implemented for p50/p95 latency and 5xx error rate, configurable per-route
Shadow traffic fork implemented that tags requests for tracing and does not affect production tokens or billing
Automatic rollback path executes within 30s of guardrail violation and is visible as a Console event with trace links
E2E test harness simulating traffic patterns and metric regressions with assertions for pause, rollback, and continue behaviors
Documentation and Console mock added to rollout editor showing TPG visualization and step override controls
notes: Motivation: existing DSLs bake steps into imperative pipelines; TPG enables richer conditional logic (early stop, staggered forks, shadow fencing) without bespoke code
We want SLO-aware transitions: rules can reference derived metrics (e.g., ratio of model A vs B latency), sliding windows, and canary-specific thresholds
Plan to reuse existing telemetry hooks (trace_id, route, model_variant tags) and extend metric collector to emit guardrail evaluation events
Aim for a minimal viable set of nodes so the schema stays compact and learnable by PMs/ops teams. We can iterate after rollout to Dedicated customers
design_decisions: Use a directed acyclic graph for the TPG to avoid non-terminating rollouts; allow explicit converge nodes to merge traffic back
Evaluate transitions at fixed heartbeat (5s) with exponential backoff for repeated evaluation to avoid metric thrash
Shadow traffic will be routed through the same serving runtime but marked with a non-billable flag and routed to isolated metrics pipeline
Rollback paths are explicit edges in the graph; in addition include a global emergency-rollback trigger that can be invoked from Console or an API
Schema will support templated variables for thresholds so projects can parametrize common policies without duplicating graphs
implementation_plan: W1: RFC + schema (owner: Aisha) and Console mockups + UX review
W2: Implement parser and core evaluator library (owner: Marco). Unit tests for node semantics
W3: Integrate evaluator with routing controller in staging; add shadow routing and non-billable flag
W4: Guardrail predicates and metrics adaptor (owner: Priya Shah). Hook into metrics service to evaluate sliding-window stats
W5: E2E harness and chaos tests; create rollback verification scenarios
W6: Docs, Console rollout editor, and internal runbook for incident response
risks: Metric lag could cause false rollbacks; mitigations: use conservative initial thresholds and require consecutive violations before rollback
Complex graphs increase operator cognitive load; mitigations: provide visual abstraction, common templates, and linting rules
Shadow traffic increases load on model hosts and metrics pipeline; mitigations: throttling, sampled shadowing, and isolated metrics ingestion
Schema changes after adoption are costly; mitigate by versioning the TPG schema and providing migration tooling
